title: mimid-agent local daemon
description: Local user-agent daemon per decision mimid-1wgh.28: MLS on-device via mimi-mls, local SQLite state; outward JMAP Chat (E2EE) + MLS capability to provider; inward plaintext JMAP Chat server on a 0600 unix socket. Decodes/encodes mimi-content <-> JMAP Message (senderMsgId per R1). Room ops: create group, invite, send/receive.
notes:
Per mimid-1wgh.30: inward plaintext JMAP Chat via crate-jmap jmap-chat-server with an MLS-backed backend impl; outward via jmap-chat-client. See ~/PROJECT/nie daemon for prior art (localhost bearer-token daemon).
2026-10-18 (mimid-1wgh.38): the agent IS the JMAP Chat bridge and there is no TUI. When planning .13, decide the inward transport so stock JMAP Chat clients can connect (loopback HTTP/WebSocket with a per-user token vs 0600 unix socket); AGENTS.md now says 'local endpoint'.
2026-10-18 (mimid-1wgh.39): plan .13 as a library crate mimid-agent-core plus a desktop daemon wrapper; keep daemon/socket/HTTP-server code out of the core so a mobile binding (epic mimid-1wgh.40) can embed it.
From F5 (2026-10-18): the server's Follower::leave() is local only. The agent's leave flow must send the MLS removal (self-remove or a Remove proposal) through the relay, then the server calls leave().
2026-10-18 (Mark): the .13 plan must include an acceptance test that unmodified stock JMAP Chat clients (crate-jmapchat-client, jmap-chat-js) work against mimid-agent, and must settle .38's open transport question (unix socket vs loopback HTTP + WebSocket/EventSource) with that test in mind. Stock clients speak HTTP, so the AGENTS.md agent-socket peer-credential boundary may need adapting (e.g. a per-user local token); that's a decision for the plan. v1 read/mute/pin state is per device (mimid-1wgh.12.29).
2026-10-18 agent requirement (crate-jmap-50, for the .13 plan): the agent fills plaintext Chat.name, description and avatar from the MLS room_metadata (protocol-06 §7.6), since provider names are empty for followed rooms, and turns a stock client's Chat/set of name/description/avatarBlobId into a room_metadata AppDataUpdate via Room/update (room policy permitting; refusals map to forbidden). The stock-client acceptance test checks that a MIMI room shows its name in crate-jmapchat-client and jmap-chat-js.
Acceptance criterion (2026-11-02, from mimid-1wgh.2.25): content-10 §3.3: before using a decoded MimiContent, reject it if its senderUri or roomUri extension is present and not byte-identical (decision mimid-1wgh.5.58) to the authenticated MLS sender URI / room URI.
2026-11-13 Mark: plan mimid-agent right after the IETF 127 hackathon (target: week of 2026-11-16) as the next milestone. The UI is jmap-chat-js through the agent's local JMAP Chat endpoint. Until then, the throwaway mimid-chat CLI (tools/interop/chat, branch tools/chat-cli) covers the weekend. Fold in what mimid-chat learns (persistent group state, Welcome pickup, polling vs push) and the client-side WhatsApp design question (mimid-9ayb).
2026-11-13 Mark: mimid-agent also serves a local IRC interface (bitlbee-style), alongside the local JMAP Chat endpoint, so stock IRC clients (irssi, weechat) become MIMI clients with E2EE intact: the MLS keys stay in the agent on the user's machine. Map channels to MIMI rooms and nicks to mimi:// user URIs. Support the IRCv3 bits that matter: echo-message, message-tags/msgid, chathistory, labeled-response, and SASL to the local agent. Keep the IRC surface in the daemon wrapper, not in mimid-agent-core (decision mimid-1wgh.39), loopback only, with a per-user token. Prior art: Mark's MeshIRCd (Go, github.com/MarkAtwood/meshIRCd: chathistory.go, ircv3.go). Either port the IRC handling to Rust or run a small Go front end against the agent's local API; decide when planning .13. Related idea (server-side gateway, not E2EE) filed in MeshIRCd's tracker.
2026-11-13 Mark: the local chat interfaces mimid-agent presents.
MUST:
1. JMAP Chat (draft-atwood-jmap-chat), native and full fidelity; for jmap-chat-js, jmap-chat-jsbig and crate-jmapchat-client.
2. IRC (bitlbee-style, IRCv3: echo-message, msgid, chathistory, labeled-response, SASL). For terminal users and bots.
NEXT:
3. XMPP client-to-server. The biggest open client ecosystem: Conversations and Monocles (Android), Monal and Siskin (iOS), Gajim, Dino, Profanity, Psi/Psi+, and every libpurple client (Pidgin, Finch, Adium, Spectrum). This is the cheapest route to mobile MIMI clients before the native app (mimid-1wgh.40). Map MUC to MIMI room and JID to mimi:// URI; modern XEPs for message ids, replies, reactions, edits, MAM history and HTTP upload. OMEMO off on the local hop, since the agent is the E2EE endpoint. For phones, the agent must run on the device or on a trusted host reached over the tailnet.
MAYBE (parked):
4. IMAP plus SMTP as a local mail server for Delta Chat. Real work: Delta Chat's own Autocrypt/OpenPGP and group semantics.
NOT:
- The Matrix client-server API (needs a whole homeserver; poor semantic fit).
- Slack-, Discord- or Telegram-compatible bot APIs (moving targets; JMAP Chat covers programmatic use).
- A native libpurple MIMI prpl (C, libpurple 2.x versus Pidgin 3's 3.x API, Adium largely unmaintained); XMPP serves all libpurple clients already.
RULES for every local interface:
- Loopback only, with a per-user token (plaintext on the local hop). Lives in the daemon wrapper, not mimid-agent-core (decision mimid-1wgh.39).
- JMAP Chat is the source of truth; each other interface is a lossy translation with documented feature limits (reactions, edits, threads, attachments).
- Sender identity always comes from the authenticated MLS sender; no interface lets a client claim another user (AGENTS.md: the agent treats everything as untrusted).
- The secrets rules apply to each interface's logging.
2026-11-13: Matrix and Beeper interop goes through a separate bridgev2 bridge, mautrix-mimi (bead filed, blocked by this one), which talks to the agent's local JMAP Chat interface. The agent still does NOT implement the Matrix client-server API; the bridge gives Beeper and any Matrix homeserver access without it.
